issues.body: `compute_ready` rejects a candidate whose packages are `{GLOBAL}` whenever `taken` contains any area (`if GLOBAL in pkgs and taken`). `frontier_census`, however, only increments `blocked` for `pkgs & held`; `{GLOBAL}` has no intersection with an area-specific held set. For example, one open PR holding `worker` plus one ready issue with no `area:` label produces `candidates=1 frontier=0 conflict-deferred=1 reserved_areas=1 free_areas=1 blocked-by-reserved: none`. The special case only handles the inverse (`GLOBAL in held`). Thus a frontier stopped by real reserved occupancy can still claim that no reservation blocks demand, and there is no self-test for this third conflict branch's census evidence.
issues.fix_hint: Account explicitly for deferred candidates containing `GLOBAL` when any non-global reservation is held, using an unambiguous bounded attribution that does not double-count, and add an exact-text self-test with an area-specific occupant and a cross-cutting ready candidate. Ensure the output cannot read `blocked-by-reserved: none` for that blocked tick.
issues.title: Cross-cutting candidates blocked by area occupancy are not attributed

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The always-emitted census and its ordinary area-conflict tests are sound, but the new attribution is incomplete for one of compute_ready's existing conflict rules: a cross-cutting candidate blocked by an area-specific occupant is counted as deferred while being attributed to no reservation. That makes a materially blocked frontier still report `blocked-by-reserved: none`, contrary to the census's stated purpose and exactness claims.
